turns.q: which customers are at risk build churn model

steps.text: I'll treat "churn" as no repeat purchase within 180 days of a customer's first order, since Olist has no subscriptions. I'm building the dataset from raw tables first.

blocks.text:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT o.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_unique_id ORDER BY purchased_at, order_id) rn
  FROM olist.fct_orders o WHERE order_status NOT IN ('canceled','unavailable')
),
first AS (SELECT * FROM v WHERE rn=1),
rep AS (
  SELECT f.customer_unique_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN v.purchased_at > f.purchased_at AND v.purchased_at <= f.purchased_at + INTERVAL 180 DAY THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) repeat180
  FROM first f JOIN v ON v.customer_unique_id=f.customer_unique_id GROUP BY 1
),
pay AS (
  SELECT order_id, MAX(installments) installments,
    MAX(CASE WHEN payment_type='credit_card' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cc,
    MAX(CASE WHEN payment_type='boleto' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) boleto,
    MAX(CASE WHEN payment_type='voucher' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) voucher
  FROM olist.fct_payments GROUP BY 1
),
cat AS (
  SELECT i.order_id, ANY_VALUE(p.category) category
  FROM olist.fct_order_items i JOIN olist.dim_products p USING(product_id) WHERE i.item_seq=1 GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT f.customer_unique_id, f.purchase_date, f.customer_state, f.order_status, f.items, f.items_value, f.freight_value,
  f.freight_value/NULLIF(f.items_value,0) freight_ratio, f.sellers, f.delivery_days, f.is_late::INT is_late, f.review_score,
  EXTRACT(dow FROM f.purchased_at) dow, EXTRACT(month FROM f.purchased_at) mth,
  p.installments, p.cc, p.boleto, p.voucher, c.category, r.repeat180
FROM first f JOIN rep r USING(customer_unique_id)
LEFT JOIN pay p USING(order_id) LEFT JOIN cat c USING(order_id)
WHERE f.purchase_date <= DATE '2018-02-28'

from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
df=churn_base.copy(); df['purchase_date']=pd.to_datetime(df['purchase_date'])
df['late_flag']=df.is_late.fillna(-1)
df['review_missing']=df.review_score.isna().astype(int)
df['delivered']=(df.order_status=='delivered').astype(int)
top_states=df.customer_state.value_counts().head(10).index
df['state_g']=np.where(df.customer_state.isin(top_states),df.customer_state,'OTHER')
top_cat=df.category.value_counts().head(25).index
df['cat_g']=np.where(df.category.isin(top_cat),df.category,'OTHER')
num=['items','items_value','freight_value','freight_ratio','sellers','delivery_days','late_flag','review_score','installments','cc','boleto','voucher','dow','mth','delivered','review_missing']
X=pd.concat([df[num],pd.get_dummies(df[['state_g','cat_g']],dtype=float)],axis=1)
y=df.repeat180
tr=df.purchase_date<'2017-10-01'; te=~tr
print(tr.sum(),te.sum(),y[tr].mean(),y[te].mean())
gb=HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_depth=3,learning_rate=0.05,max_iter=200,l2_regularization=1.0,random_state=0).fit(X[tr],y[tr])
p=gb.predict_proba(X[te])[:,1]
print('GB AUC',roc_auc_score(y[te],p),'AP',average_precision_score(y[te],p))
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
lr=make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy='median'),StandardScaler(),LogisticRegression(C=0.1,max_iter=500)).fit(X[tr],y[tr])
pl=lr.predict_proba(X[te])[:,1]
print('LR AUC',roc_auc_score(y[te],pl),'AP',average_precision_score(y[te],pl))
t=df[te].copy(); t['p']=p
t['decile']=pd.qcut(t.p.rank(method='first'),10,labels=False)+1
d=t.groupby('decile').agg(customers=('p','size'),repeat_rate=('repeat180','mean'),avg_score=('p','mean')).reset_index()
print(d)
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
pi=permutation_importance(gb,X[te],y[te],scoring='roc_auc',n_repeats=3,random_state=0)
imp=pd.Series(pi.importances_mean,index=X.columns).sort_values(ascending=False).head(8); print(imp)
# simple segment rates
for c in ['late_flag','review_score','boleto']:
    print(df.groupby(c).repeat180.agg(['mean','size']))
result=d;

turns.answer:
Almost every customer is "at risk", and the model can't reliably tell them apart: **97.2% of customers never reorder within 180 days**. The holdout AUC is only **0.57 to 0.59**, close to a coin flip [2].

- **Setup:** I defined churn as no repeat order within 180 days of a person's first order, with first orders through Feb 2018 (56,630 people) [1]. I trained on earlier cohorts and tested on Oct 2017 to Feb 2018 [2].
- **Lift:** The top score decile reorders at 4.4% and the bottom at 2.2%, about 2x [2]. Installments, freight share and category matter slightly. Lateness and review score barely matter.
- **Action:** Treat this as acquisition-and-retention economics, not a risk list. A better churn model needs more history per customer, which this data lacks.

Caveat: Olist has no subscriptions, so "churn" here means a missed repeat purchase. Sep and Oct 2018 are excluded as incomplete.
